1. What Are Tesla's (TSLA) Main Competitors? - Investopedia
   In the electric vehicle (EV) market, one name has long dominated headlines and has often been synonymous with EVs in the public mind: Tesla ([TSLA](https://www.investopedia.com/markets/quote?tvwidgetsymbol=TSLA)). Founded in 1995 as a battery manufacturer, BYD has leveraged its expertise in energy storage to compete with Tesla as the leader in worldwide EV sales each [quarter](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/q/quarter.asp). A pandemic-era slump and other industry shifts meant companies like Hertz ([HTZ](https://www.investopedia.com/markets/quote?tvwidgetsymbol=HTZ)) started selling off thousands of their Tesla EVs, putting these bargain-priced alternatives in competition with Tesla’s new vehicles—enough that if they counted as new cars, they would be among Tesla’s top three competitors in 2024.19. This is among the reasons Tesla’s market capitalization is so many times greater than that of companies like Ford and GM, whose [sales](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/122214/what-difference-between-revenue-and-sales.asp) dwarf Teslas. In May 2024, Biden also increased [tariffs](https://www.investopedia.com/terms/t/tariff.asp) on Chinese EVs from 25%—the amount Trump had assigned during his first presidential administration—to 100%, protecting Tesla from an onslaught of Chinese vehicles entering the U.S. market. *   [How can electric vehicle technology expand into new market segments?](https://www.investopedia.com/ask/answers/120314/who-are-teslas-tsla-main-competitors.asp#).
